note: Ready-made routes. Each is a sequence, not a list — the order matters, and the timings assume you leave home at the stated hour.

items.title: Saturday Morning on Your Own Doorstep
items.why: The mission you can do in slippers. Note the trap: Du Pain et des Idées, the best bakery near you, is closed at weekends — so the weekend route goes to Mamiche instead, and you save the other one for a weekday morning.

stops.text: Coffee at Ten Belles, rue de la Grange aux Belles
Babka at Mamiche, rue du Château d'Eau
Browse La Trésorerie for the flat — the best homewares shop in Paris
Marché Saint-Quentin for the week's food, and a glass of wine at the bar in the middle
Finish at Artazart on the canal, then sit on the water

items.title: The Rainy Day Route
items.why: Almost the entire route is under glass. When it is raining and you refuse to spend the day indoors, this is the answer — four 19th-century arcades chained together, with second-hand bookshops, stamp dealers, an old walking-cane maker and tea rooms. Ends at a free museum with a garden café.

stops.text: Start at Grands Boulevards
Passage des Panoramas — the oldest arcade in Paris, 1799
Cross the boulevard to Passage Jouffroy, then Passage Verdeau for old books and cameras
Lunch in one of the passage bistros
Walk to Galerie Vivienne — mosaic floors, the beautiful one
Finish at Musée de la Vie Romantique: free, and tea in the glass conservatory

items.title: The Perfect Sunday: Market, Picnic, Viaduct
items.priceNote: ~€20 for a very good picnic for two
items.why: The single best use of a sunny Sunday in Paris, and it costs almost nothing. Buy lunch at the best market in the city, then eat it four metres above the street on a garden built along a disused railway. Go early — Aligre is finished by 13:30.

stops.text: M8 to Ledru-Rollin
Marché Beauvau covered hall — cheese, charcuterie, olives
The open-air market outside for fruit; prices drop as they pack up
Ten minutes in the little flea market on the square — people sell genuinely odd things
Madeleines from Blé Sucré, rue Antoine Vollon
Up onto the Coulée verte at Bastille and walk east through the rose arches
Picnic on a bench above the street, then carry on to the Jardin de Reuilly

items.title: After-Work Sunset, Cheap and Perfect
items.priceNote: A bottle from a caviste + cheap dinner
items.why: The best free view in Paris, eighteen minutes from home, with none of the crowd at Sacré-Cœur. Buy the wine before you go up — there is nothing at the top. Then walk down into Belleville, which has the cheapest good food in the city.

stops.text: Buy a bottle and two plastic cups near Couronnes
Up to the top terrace of Parc de Belleville — arrive 40 min before sunset
Come down through rue Denoyez for the street art
Dinner on rue de Belleville — Chinese, Vietnamese or North African, all excellent, all cheap

items.title: You Have Never Really Explored the 13th
items.why: The 13th is the arrondissement people in the 10th most reliably neglect, and it has a hilltop village, an art deco swimming pool fed by a natural spring, thirteen-storey murals, streets named after flowers, and the best Asian food in France. One direct Metro line from you.

stops.text: M7 direct to Corvisart
The street art circuit — start with the murals around boulevard Vincent Auriol
Up into La Butte-aux-Cailles: cobbles, ivy, low houses, no cars
Swim in the 1920s Piscine de la Butte-aux-Cailles, artesian spring water, about €4
La Cité Florale — five tiny streets named after flowers, all hollyhocks and cottages
Late lunch on avenue de Choisy — the Vietnamese here is the real thing

items.title: One Trip, Whole Day: La Villette
items.why: Everything on this route is on one site, twenty-two minutes from you on line 5, and half of it is free. The trick is the timing: exhibition in the afternoon, canal-side drink as the light goes, then lie on the grass for a film at 21:00. You do not move more than 500 metres after 15:00.

stops.text: M5 to Porte de Pantin
Beyond the Streets at the Grande Halle — 3,600 m² of graffiti and street art
Drink on the Bassin de la Villette terraces as it cools down
Get a spot on the Prairie du Triangle by 20:15 with a blanket
Free open-air film at 21:00 under the stars
Walk home down the canal if the night is warm — 40 minutes, and worth it

items.title: The Secret Village Twenty Minutes Away
items.why: Most people go to Buttes-Chaumont and stop there. Behind it is the Mouzaïa — a grid of cobbled private lanes of rose-covered cottages, built cheap in the 1900s because old gypsum mines underneath meant nothing heavy could be built on top. You will not believe you are in Paris, and it is fifteen minutes from your flat.

stops.text: M7bis to Botzaris
Into Buttes-Chaumont, up to the temple on the rock for the view
Cross the suspension bridge, out of the north-east gate
The Mouzaïa villas — rue de Mouzaïa, Villa de Bellevue, Villa des Lilas
Coffee tasting at Brûlerie de Belleville if it is open

items.title: Design Crawl for the Flat
items.priceNote: Free to browse, dangerous to your wallet
items.why: If you want to make the flat nicer, this is the densest concentration of good independent design shops in Paris, all within a ten-minute radius of each other in the north Marais, with the oldest covered market in the city in the middle of it for lunch.

stops.text: Walk, or M8 to Filles du Calvaire
Empreintes — four floors of contemporary French craft, free to visit
Ofr. for art books and independent magazines
Lunch in the Marché des Enfants Rouges — arrive before 12:30 for a seat
Merci and the shops along rue Charlot and rue de Poitou
Green Factory for a terrarium on the way home

items.title: Flea Market Dawn Raid
items.priceNote: Bring cash — €30 goes a long way
items.why: The unglamorous truth about flea markets is that everything good is gone by ten. Vanves is the one worth the early alarm: real people selling from trestle tables, prices you can haggle, silver cutlery and old linen and ceramics. It shuts at 14:00 sharp. Then a park and lunch to recover.

stops.text: M13 to Porte de Vanves — leave home by 08:00
Work avenue Marc Sangnier first, then Georges Lafenestre
Coffee and regroup, then a second pass — sellers soften after 11:00
Parc Montsouris to sit down with your finds
Lunch on rue Daguerre, a pedestrian market street that feels like a village

items.title: A Night Out Without Leaving the 10th
items.why: The whole night is within a fifteen-minute walk of your door, which means no last-Metro maths and no taxi. Faubourg Saint-Denis is the best drinking street in Paris and almost nobody outside the neighbourhood has worked that out yet.

stops.text: Start with a glass at Le Verre Volé, rue de Lancry
Eat early and cheap in Passage Brady, or on rue du Faubourg Saint-Denis
Cocktails at Le Syndicat — everything French, behind the fly-posted door
Whatever is on at New Morning, five minutes away
If it is Thursday to Saturday and you are still going: La Java
Walk home along the canal

items.title: One Street, Three Jazz Clubs
items.why: Rue des Lombards has three serious jazz clubs within eighty metres of each other, which makes it the one place in Paris where you can turn up without a booking and still hear something excellent. Sets run twice a night, so you can do two clubs in one evening.

stops.text: M4 to Châtelet
Early dinner in the Montorgueil streets, ten minutes north
First set at Duc des Lombards, 19:30 — the serious one
Second set next door at Sunset/Sunside or Le Baiser Salé, 21:30
If you want to dance, Caveau de la Huchette is fifteen minutes across the river and runs till 02:00
